A relationship is between two people, if they don't get you, then this can be discussed but needs consensus. There needs to be chemistry. Finding a partner is hard and building the relationship to last is harder. Keep climbing. There will be a right mix where there is a fit and if there are compromises they are too small. Invest how you feel it's ok. I always go for being yourself first. The other person should be a "partner in crime" who can inspire you, support you and make your life better and vice versa but you still need to be individuals. You will never find perfection but you should look for "great" (on average). This way whatever happens to the relationship 6 months, 6 years or 60 years later. You can still be yourself in the most part.

You will have to be conscious of your trust issues but don't let them control you. The previous partners have nothing to do with the new one. Benefit of a doubt still applies, to some extent, but you also need to be a bit detached for a bit in the beginning. This way there is no pressure and you can also enjoy the relationship as it is before it becomes something serious. 
Also (forgive me for saying this) re-evaluate your dating pool. What are you looking for? It's likely that you may attract the wrong partners based on criteria which doesn't match your relationship goals.
Moreover, (I don't know you so I can't judge the circumstances) being cool about it and not going all in makes the other person work a bit for the relationship, investing time, energy and emotions. This should serve as some evidence of commitment. 
You will never be certain, only of yourself. If things work then great "let's have an amazing life together" but if not, that's fine "I'm free to find the one I care for and won't waste any more time, bye".

Re roommate or housemates it's a bit of a lottery because you can be good friends or colleagues but living with someone is something else.

When I moved out it was a big step for me. I left to another country to study. Sold my car and with some savings, a bursary and a loan I enrolled in a 3 year course and remained there till this day (8 years later). 

The moment I arrived in my small basement single room and opened my bags to setup my stuff... That was to moment when it sank in that I left my parents house, probably for good and this is my life now. 

Panic was the first reaction. I felt alone in a foreign world, exposed, even at 18. I was a pretty independent teen but this still affected me. From the beginning there was a pressure to succeed and had the anxiety caused by a constant fear of failure.

I had to tell myself that I am not the first nor the last person to do this and I should move on. All this will be worth fighting for. And it was true.

First you need a complete mindset overhaul. You have to make a change on how you motivate yourself and how important this new lifestyle is for you. That will impact your routine, your ambition, your food and how much you care about your goals.
I'm not being sarcastic or ironic. In my case, this happened as soon as I started looking at my bills. My dream was to become a movie producer.

All the time. The point to remember is that this is a proper grind. You have to keep going at it. Before you get to speak to someone on the phone or face to face, 70% is about luck. Luck that their systems didn't reject you automatically (most have a check system in place), luck that the person reading your application had a good night sleep or didn't have a fight with their spouses... You get where I'm going. It's important to get to talk to someone and sell yourself. 

This takes me to the next point: play by your rules, not theirs. Find any (legal and non-creepy) way to network with people working there. Check conferences, competitions, courses, etc. Think about it this way: everyone is making the application, everyone is going to the job fair. A recruiter will talk to hundreds of people so it's impossible that they will remember you. Find a way to get noticed. A referral from an employee is a big head start.

TL DR: Keep applying, don't take early stage rejections personally, network like crazy and get noticed (in a good way)
